}}The '''Great Imperial War''',{{efn|Often abbreviated as '''GIW''' or '''IW'''}} or the '''First Great War''' (7th April 1661 – 29th September 1666), also known as the '''Imperial War''', was a [[Wikipedia:World war|global conflict]] between two [[Wikipedia:Coalitions|coalitions]]: the [[Lasen Powers of the Great Imperial War|Lasen's]] and the [[Middle Powers]]. Major areas of conflict included [[Ayuma]], [[Massir]], as well as parts of [[Acrola]], [[Mahea]] and [[Quia]]. The war saw important developments in weaponry including [[Wikipedia:Tanks|tanks]], [[Wikipedia:Aviation|aircraft]], [[Wikipedia:Artillery|artillery]], machine guns, and [[Wikipedia:Chemical weapons|chemical weapons]]. One of the [[List of wars by death toll|deadliest conflicts in history]], it resulted in an estimated [[World War I casualties|25 million military casualties]], and 7 million civilian deaths from war-related causes and [[Genocides in history|genocide]].<ref name="factbook-giw">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/events/great-imperial-war|title=The Great Imperial War (1661–1666): Overview|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=14 February 1764}}</ref><ref name="ahr-casualties">{{cite web|url=https://www.andahhistoricalreview.org/articles/great-imperial-war-casualties|title=Counting the Dead: Casualty Estimates of the Great Imperial War|publisher=Andah Historical Review|date=9 August 1763}}</ref>

The [[causes of the Great Imperial War]] included the rise of the [[Estijan Huan]] and decline of the [[Merelan Empire]] which disturbed the long-standing [[Wikipedia:Balance of power (international relations)|balance of power]] in Ayuma, the exacerbation of imperial rivalries, and an intensive arms race between the [[Wikipedia:Great power|great powers]].<ref name="factbook-causes">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/events/great-imperial-war/causes|title=The Great Imperial War: Origins and the Ayuman Balance of Power|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=3 May 1763}}</ref> The beggining of the [[Tiesa Crisis]] started after [[Emara]] blocked [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] shipping vesels from crossing the [[Tiesa Canal]], [[Easuhura]] begun to publicly call for the freedom of movement through the canal noting it was "non-negotiable": [[Lycroa]] sent a naval escort, composed of vessels from a fleet anchoring at Trisande. [[Kingdom of Alzuria|Alzuria]] offered mediation but failed to develop any diplomatic compromises. Growing tensions between [[Emara]] and [[Easuhura]] finally reached a breaking point on the 5th of April 1661 when the [[SSA-Tansirah]] an [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] destroyer, was sunk after a miscommunication in fog.<ref name="archives-tiesa">{{cite web|url=https://archives.easuhura.gov.eu/great-imperial-war/tiesa-crisis|title=The Tiesa Crisis and the Sinking of the SSA-Tansirah|publisher=National Archives of Easuhura|date=22 June 1762}}</ref> [[Easuhura]] blamed [[Emara]] and vice versa. Both nations had declared war on each other, two days later, on the 7th. After [[Lycroa]] and [[Praesyu]] mobilized in [[Easuhura]]'s defense, Estijan declared war on Verusa. Prompting Lycroa, who had [[Lycroan-Verusan Alliance|an alliance]] with Verusa, to declare war on Estijan. The [[Kingdom of Alzuria]] entered the war after [[Estijan Huan]] invoked a [[Alzurian-Estijan defense agreement| Defense agreement]], and Hkuqo joined the [[Middle Powers]] in January 1662. [[Lycroa|Lycroa's]] strategy in 1661 was to quickly push into [[Siana]] while linking with [[Verusa]], swiftly defeat [[Siana]] before transferring its forces to the south, avoiding the defences across the Emaran Border, but its advance was halted in May, and by the end of the year the [[Western Front (Great Imperial War)|Western Front]] consisted of [[Wikipedia:Trench warfare|a near-continuous line of trenches]] from the [[Escaran Channel]] to [[Palina]].<ref name="ahr-westernfront">{{cite web|url=https://www.andahhistoricalreview.org/articles/great-imperial-war-western-front|title=Stalemate in the West: The Trench Line of 1661|publisher=Andah Historical Review|date=17 October 1762}}</ref> The [[Eastern Front (World War I)|Northern Front]] and [[Southern front]] was more dynamic, but neither side gained a decisive advantage, despite launching several costly offensives. [[Merela Sta]], [[Yaxuto]], [[Darewa]] and others entered the war from 1664 onward.

Major battles, including those at [[Liamvra]], [[Khalviro]], and [[Louttan]], failed to break the stalemate on the Western and northern fronts.<ref name="factbook-battles">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/events/great-imperial-war/major-battles|title=The Great Imperial War: Major Battles of the Western and Northern Fronts|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=28 January 1763}}</ref> In February 1664, the [[American entry into World War I| Kingdom of Alzuria]] was severely crippled from the war after the Middle Powers resumed [[Unrestricted submarine warfare (February 1917)|unrestricted submarine warfare]] against Nasuanian Sea shipping. Later that year, the [[Shiry ibn]] seized power in [[Alzuria (region)|Alzuria]] in the [[Alzurian Revolution]]; signing an armistice with the Middle Powers in May, followed by [[Treaty of Brest-Litovsk|a separate peace]] in June 1664.<ref name="archives-alzuria">{{cite web|url=https://archives.alzuria.gov.az/great-imperial-war/revolution-and-armistice|title=The Alzurian Revolution and the Separate Peace of 1664|publisher=National Archives of Alzuria|date=11 December 1761}}</ref> That month, Emara launched an [[autumn offensive in the west]], which left the Lycroan Army exhausted and demoralized. The [[Kuwana Dyasty]] joined the war in August 1664, with the invasion of [[Hijita]] in July 1665, which caused a collapse of the Verusan front line. Following the [[Shyfa Offensive,]] Yaxuto signed [[Armistice of Salonica|an armistice]] in early September. By mid-September, the [[Lasen powers|Lasen]] had signed armistices with [[Lycroa]] and [[Praesyu]], leaving Easuhura isolated. Facing [[German revolution of 1918–1919|a revolution at home]], [[Abdication of Humrai Shah|Humrai Shah abdicated]] on 28th of September, and the war ended with the [[Armistice of 29th September 1666]].<ref name="factbook-armistice">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/events/great-imperial-war/armistice|title=The Abdication of Humrai Shah and the Armistice of 29 September 1666|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=6 March 1764}}</ref>

The [[Rivostan Peace Conference]] of 1665–1666 imposed settlements on the defeated powers. Under the [[Treaty of Versailles|Treaty of Kiishi]] (more commonly called the Treaty of Fraud), [[Verusa]], [[Lycroa]] and [[Easuhura]] all suffered similar fates, and lost significant Ayuman territories, along with most of their overseas colonies, were disarmed, and were required to pay large [[Wikipedia:War reparations|war reparations]] to the Lasen's with.<ref name="factbook-kiishi">{{cite web|url=https://www.theandahfactbook.org/events/treaty-of-kiishi|title=The Treaty of Kiishi and the Rivostan Peace Conference|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=19 April 1763}}</ref> [[Hijita]] was given to [[Ashain]] in return for an armistice, since they were the only Middle power still able to fight. The Lasen powers led interventions to maintain the treaty and uphold world peace, including the [[Dahe Chaos]], [[Azlurian Civil War|Azlurian]], [[Lycroan Civil War |Lycroan Civil Wars]], and [[Uularin Rebellion]]. Its poorly planned interventions and failure to manage these conflicts contributed to the outbreak of the [[Red War]] in 1687.<ref name="ahr-aftermath">{{cite web|url=https://www.andahhistoricalreview.org/articles/great-imperial-war-aftermath|title=From the Treaty of Kiishi to the Red War: The Failed Peace, 1666–1687|publisher=Andah Historical Review|date=30 November 1763}}</ref>
